- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if history shows downward trend.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to post-spike values.
- Mean reversion is evident: if forecast is far above true outcome (e.g., >2x), reduce by 15–30% in next 7d window; if below, increase by 10–20%.
- Forecasts for 30d horizon are often too optimistic in bullish sentiment periods; cap forecast at 1.5x historical 30d mean if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast spikes.
